scenes.title: Early Holocene & Paleoindian corridors: volcanic glass, flint & Pacific shell
scenes.body: By 7000 BCE, Arctic hunters carried Batza Téna obsidian north across Alaska; Northwest canoes moved Mount Edziza glass down the Stikine; Cascade crossings carried Newberry obsidian to Oregon shores; California Olivella beads crossed the Sierra into Nevada caves; and Alca obsidian reached Peru's desert coast.
scenes.note: Arrows connect geological quarry zones or shell habitats to excavated find spots active at 7000 BCE; earlier 10,800 BCE Knife River and Alibates Clovis networks appear in the shared timeline.

scenes.title: Old Copper, Labrador chert, Pacific abalone/Spondylus & Amazonian cacao
scenes.body: By the third millennium BCE, Archaic miners around Lake Superior forged cold-hammered copper reaching coastal graves; Maritime Archaic mariners carried Labrador Ramah chert over 1,500 km to Maine; and Ecuadorian traders moved warm-water Spondylus southward to Caral-Supe alongside Upper Amazonian Theobroma cacao.
scenes.note: Points stay strictly within the 2200 BCE calibrated context intervals for each sourced material.

scenes.title: Poverty Point's continental web, Olmec jadeite mirrors & early Chavín
scenes.body: Around 1100 BCE, monumental networks peaked simultaneously across three subcontinents: Louisiana's Poverty Point amassed Ouachita quartz, Missouri galena, and Gulf shell; Olmec Veracruz imported Motagua jadeite and Oaxaca magnetite mirrors; and Peru's Chavín de Huántar gathered Ecuadorian conch trumpets alongside Ayacucho Quispisisa glass and Huancavelica cinnabar.
scenes.note: Each arrow summarizes cited provenance research active at 1100 BCE rather than implying unified continental governance.

scenes.title: Adena pipestone, Preclassic Maya obsidian, Andean caravans & Antilles beads
scenes.body: By 500 BCE, highland llama caravans hauled Chivay and Quispisisa obsidian and Atacama turquoise across Andean passes, Preclassic Maya and Zapotec centers moved El Chayal and Pachuca obsidian, Adena mounds circulated Ohio pipestone, and Saladoid canoeists began sailing exotic South American nephrite and amethyst north up the Antilles.
scenes.note: All shown lines represent active stratigraphic intervals crossing 500 BCE.

scenes.title: 1 CE: Hopewell's 2,500-km Interaction Sphere, Bering Strait & Puerto Rico
scenes.body: At the threshold of the Common Era, the Hopewell Interaction Sphere united Yellowstone obsidian, Ontario Cobalt silver, North Carolina mica, Lake Superior copper, and Florida Gulf whelk in Ohio earthworks—while Bering Strait Norton sailors imported Siberian obsidian, Maya canoes moved Ixtepeque glass, and Vieques workshops carved Guiana–Orinoco greenstones.
scenes.note: Viewing year 1 CE highlights documented active contexts intersecting the turn of the era (all <= 100 CE in this focused expansion).
